faq.q: What is the International Date Line?
faq.a: It is an imaginary line, mostly along 180 degrees longitude in the Pacific Ocean, where the calendar date changes. Places just west of it are a day ahead of places just east of it.

faq.q: What happens when you cross the Date Line?
faq.a: Travelling west across it, you add a day, so Monday becomes Tuesday. Travelling east, you go back a day, so Tuesday becomes Monday again.
asks: Do you lose a day when you cross the Date Line?

faq.q: Why does the Date Line zigzag?
faq.a: It bends round island groups so that one country is not split into two different dates. Kiribati had it moved in 1995 so all its islands share the same day.
asks: Why is the Date Line not straight?

faq.q: Why did Samoa skip a day in 2011?
faq.a: Samoa moved from the east side to the west side of the Date Line to share working days with Australia and New Zealand, its big trading partners. So Thursday 29 December 2011 was followed straight by Saturday 31 December.
asks: Why did Samoa skip a day?

faq.q: Where does each new day start first?
faq.a: New days begin just west of the Date Line. Kiribati’s Line Islands, 14 hours ahead of UTC, are among the first places on Earth to see each new date.
asks: Which country sees the new year first?

facts: Samoa skipped Friday 30 December 2011 when it moved to the west side of the Date Line.
Kiribati's Line Islands use UTC+14, the earliest time zone on Earth.

quiz.say: You fly east from Japan across the Date Line to Hawaii. What happens to the date?
quiz.show: Crossing the Date Line going east, the date…
quiz.why: Going east across the line, you move from the day-ahead side to the day-behind side, so the date goes back one day.

wrong.1: Jumping forward happens when you cross going west.
wrong.2: Crossing the line always changes the date by one day.

quiz.say: Why is the Date Line in the Pacific Ocean, near 180 degrees?
quiz.show: The Date Line is near 180 degrees because…

options.show: It is halfway round from Greenwich, where few people live
options.say: It is halfway round from Greenwich, where few people live

options.show: It is where the Earth stops spinning
options.say: It is where the Earth stops spinning

options.show: It is the hottest part of the ocean
options.say: It is the hottest part of the ocean

quiz.why: At 180 degrees, east and west of Greenwich meet, and putting the line in the open ocean splits very few places.

wrong.2: The line has nothing to do with temperature.
